comment: Checks this plugin can run against a USER'S repo, for project_gates.py to discover.
A plugin declares its own; the runner never hardcodes a list, so adding a check here is the
whole registration step and a new plugin needs no change to the runner.
applies_when: every path must exist in the user's repo, or the check reports NOT APPLICABLE
with that reason. An empty list means it always applies. Not-applicable is never a pass.
A path nothing writes is therefore a PERMANENT not-applicable -- a gate that cannot fail, and
indistinguishable from one that correctly found nothing to do. scripts/check_manifest_paths.py
reconciles every path below against the paths this plugin's own scripts and commands name (#423).
requires: executables that must be on PATH. Missing is a FAILURE, not a skip -- in CI a skip
is indistinguishable from a pass unless something asserts the dependency is there.

checks.why: A plan that crosses a security boundary, changes structure, the data model or a dependency, or spans six or more components needs a recorded Fable `plan-advisor` pass with every finding disposed, for the plan as it is now (#2262, owner direction: everything must be enforced). The stop gate checks it at the end of a turn; this registration makes the sweep that `gh pr ready` requires check it too, so a PR cannot be marked ready past a skipped advisory. RETHINK blocks until a fresh pass says PROCEED or a named override is recorded. The branch decides the unit; a branch with no plan files owes nothing. applies_when is `docs`, not the two criteria homes: every listed path must exist, and the layout's `docs/product/acceptance` and the pre-layout `docs/acceptance` are alternatives (#2267 plan-advisor A-6).

A project gets the gates and, until now, no proof they work. When this was added, every shipped check script carried a --selftest and no consumer gate entry ran one. Upstream, mutation coverage is the only reason any of it is trusted, and it caught four gates written that same day being partly vacuous -- none of that machinery crosses into a project. This runs every shipped selftest HERE, which is the one question the toolchain's own CI is structurally unable to answer: our CI proves a check discriminates on our machine, never on yours. A FAILING selftest means the GATE is broken in this project -- it may have rotted against a framework or Python version we do not have -- and is routed to the toolchain, never filed against your code.
Acceptance criteria that cannot fail grade nothing. Criteria live at docs/product/acceptance/<slug>.md under the shipped layout; the pre-layout docs/acceptance/ is still matched (#910).
A work order an executor cannot run from is not self-contained. It lives at docs/product/handoff/<slug>.md under the shipped layout; the pre-layout docs/handoff/ is still matched (#1700).
A brief that copies its own PRD is a second source of truth, and a citation that resolves to nothing reads as traceable while carrying nothing.
A guide whose steps nobody can re-run is a sentiment.
The graph is regenerated at session end; a stale one describes an app that no longer exists.

Three memory systems can inject into every session and none knows about the others; a project that says nothing in its committed settings loads whatever each user enabled globally. This holds the loaded set to the one the project recorded, at no per-session cost.
A gem the doctrine marks Always, with no installer and no gate, is a preference — it landed missing twice on two clean runs.

CLAUDE.md is loaded by every session and accretes incident narrative until an agent skims it; past its recorded ceiling, or with none recorded, the check says which paragraphs to relocate — verbatim, never summarised.

docs/brain is the team's memory and Claude Code's auto-memory is what a session loads at start; a lesson in one and not the other is either unshared or unrecalled. Counts both directions; n/a without a brain or a store; nothing is written.

The SessionStart nudge 'brain-review due since 2026-10-04' printed for 18 days and nothing acted on it, so docs/brain/STATUS.md sat on 2026-09-27 while seven owner rulings lived in one session's memory (#2297). A nudge is not enforcement: this refuses an ARM or a PROMOTION while STATUS.md's `_Updated: <date> · sha` commit is older than the newest v* tag's commit. It fires only at an arm (a chore/arm-* or release/* branch, or a diff that adds a `(release vX.Y.Z)` heading to CHANGELOG.md) and is not applicable otherwise, so it does not turn every PR red between a release and the refresh. At an arm it cannot be 'unable to tell': a STATUS it cannot read, a sha the clone lacks or a shallow clone is a refusal, never a pass.

A file's directory answers the question a reader would ask to find it; without a map agents litter docs/ and nothing can say a file is misplaced. Reports root files, code in docs, binaries at a root, product content inside the brain, memos at the brain root, and the missing map; --propose prints the moves with their link rewrites.

docs/wiki's reference pages are a join over the architecture graph, db/schema.rb, the queue configs and the lockfiles; a page that no longer matches its sources is a transcription that rotted. n/a until the graph exists, and until the wiki is first built.

With .rails-flow/generated-docs.json declared, a branch outside `enforce_on` must not modify the generated docs (docs/architecture/, docs/wiki/) at all: committed generated files conflicted on every parallel PR, and every merge re-conflicted every other open one (#1230). The drift checks only warn on such a branch; this is what stops it regenerating them anyway. n/a without the policy file.

Every column in db/schema.rb, and in every other db/*_schema.rb a second database dumps (not the Solid trio, except that a Solid table the inventory NAMES is read and its listed entries judged, its unlisted columns exempt, #1732), is classified in config/privacy_inventory.yml (table -> column -> {category, basis, retention}; `category: none` for not personal). The privacy policy is drafted from this file, so an unclassified personal column is one the policy silently omits (#1310).

No MCP tool result carries a personal category it was not allowed. Each class-form tool declares what its result is built from (`sources: %w[table.column ...]`); every column, and every sum/avg/min/max of one, is held to config/privacy_inventory.yml, and a category other than `none` needs an allow-list entry for that tool in .rails-flow/mcp.json. An undeclared tool can return anything, so it is a finding (#1931, gate 3 of #1885). Read from declarations, so it runs in CI with no app booted.

Every MCP tool sets read_only_hint and open_world_hint explicitly. Unset, the 2026-07-28 schema's defaults describe a destructive, open-world tool, and the mcp gem fills every other hint with those defaults the moment any one is declared, so only the source can tell stated from defaulted (#1882, umbrella #1306). Annotations are not inherited by a subclass, so each concrete tool states its own.

A migration numbered at or below the base branch's schema version is recorded as applied and never runs, so its columns never arrive and the suite fails somewhere unrelated. The rule lived only in /rails-flow:coordinate, so nothing ordinary checked it; downstream a branch merged dev, db:schema:load stamped schema.rb past its migration, and the column silently vanished (#1248).

A dev → main promotion must be a merge commit: a squash keeps the content and drops the ancestry, and the NEXT promotion cannot merge. `gh pr merge --merge` is doctrine a human can forget at the Merge button; a GitHub ruleset on the release branch (PRs merge only, no deletion, no force-push) is the mechanism. n/a off GitHub or on a private repository whose plan has no rulesets (GitHub's 403 "Upgrade to GitHub Pro" answer); an error (could not check) without gh, unauthenticated, or when the rulesets cannot be read (#1872).

The in-app Help & SOP is a join over docs/product/help/ (procedures, rules, glossary and screen guides, each citing its spec section) and docs/product/help/registry.json (the app's own dump of its settings, permissions and screens). A setting, permission or screen with no Help entry, a procedure with no citation, or a build that no longer matches its sources fails; explanation belongs in Help, not the interface, and Help must describe the deployed app. n/a until the registry exists, and until Help is first built (#934).

A requirement registry row that still points at a closed issue as partial or missing makes the status report show fixed gaps as open (#1853); the PR that closes an issue updates the rows that point at it.

A threat model (#2117) says what a unit must resist; a model nobody verified is a claim. When the change adds or edits docs/security/threat-models/<slug>.md, `security-auditor` must have answered every mitigate and accept row, citing an existing file:line for each implemented control, in a record tied to this HEAD (docs/evidence/reviews/prs/<slug>/security-audit.md). A missing or stale record, a mitigate row not implemented, or an accept row gone stale fails the sweep, and gh pr ready needs a green sweep (#2119).
